extracted.intended_audience: LTCH administrators, hospital coders, Medicare policy analysts, Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs), and other stakeholders in Medicare payment policy
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and regulatory requirements for calculating FY2027 MS-LTC-DRG classifications and relative weights under the Long-Term Care Hospital (LTCH) Prospective Payment System (PPS), including data preparation, trimming rules, the HSRV iterative calculation, handling low/no-volume DRGs, caps, and budget neutrality adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: HIPAA transaction and code set compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must comply with the adopted transaction standards and operating rules specified in subparts I through S of 45 CFR part 162; on or after January 1, 2012, covered entities are required to use the ASC X12 Standards for Electronic Data Interchange Technical Report Type 3—Health Care Claim: Institutional (837) (ASC X12N/005010X223 and ASC X12N/005010X233A1) for health care claims or equivalent encounter information transactions (45 CFR 162.1102(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the required electronic transaction formats and operating rules for submitting claims used in the claims processing/GROUPER/MAC workflows described in this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon discharge LTCHs must assign appropriate diagnosis and procedure codes from ICD-10-CM for diagnosis coding and ICD-10-PCS for inpatient hospital procedure coding, both of which were required to be implemented October 1, 2015 (45 CFR 162.1002(c)(2) and (3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional coding instructions and examples are published in AHA's Coding Clinic for ICD-10-CM/PCS and in referenced preamble sections; proposed changes to ICD-10-CM/PCS affect GROUPER and MS-LTC-DRG assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: MS-DRG/MS-LTC-DRG severity subdivision by CC/MCC
rubrics_metrics.description: Base DRGs are subdivided according to presence of specific secondary diagnoses designated as complications or comorbidities (CCs) into one, two, or three levels of severity depending on impact on resources; three-level splits correspond to without CC/MCC, with CC, and with MCC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Severity subdivisions should reflect increasing resource use and thus relative weights should monotonically increase by severity within a base DRG; see Step 7 for nonmonotonicity handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims screening and classification (MCE and GROUPER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs) enter clinical and demographic information from LTCH submissions into claims processing systems and subject it to automated screening called the Medicare Code Editor (MCE). After MCE screening, each claim is classified into the appropriate MS-LTC-DRG by the Medicare LTCH GROUPER software based on diagnosis/procedure codes and demographic info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain cases selected by MCE may require further review; GROUPER Version changes and MCE changes affect assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for LTCH review of MS-LTC-DRG assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the LTCH PPS, LTCHs have an opportunity to review MS-LTC-DRG assignments made by the MAC and to submit additional information within a specified timeframe as provided in § 412.513(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural requirement supports accuracy of final MS-LTC-DRG assignments used for payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three volume-based MS-LTC-DRG categories
rubrics_metrics.description: For relative weight determination MS-LTC-DRGs are categorized as: (1) MS-LTC-DRGs with at least 25 applicable LTCH cases assigned a unique relative weight; (2) low-volume MS-LTC-DRGs with 1–24 applicable LTCH cases grouped into quintiles and assigned the quintile relative weight; and (3) no-volume MS-LTC-DRGs cross-walked to other MS-LTC-DRGs and assigned that relative weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This categorization drives whether an MS-LTC-DRG receives a direct calculated weight, a quintile weight, or a cross-walked weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 — Prepare data (select and group applicable claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and group applicable claims data used for developing MS-LTC-DRG relative weights (for FY2027 they used total charges from FY2025 MedPAR Dec 2025 update and proposed GROUPER Version 44). Use better/final data if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with historical practice, only use applicable LTCH cases: trim claims paid the site neutral payment rate (or that would have been) and exclude all-inclusive rate providers, LTCHs paid under demonstration projects, and Medicare Advantage (Part C) claims (identified by GHO Paid indicator = '1'). For dual-rate methodology, include only cases meeting criteria for exclusion from site neutral payment rate (or that would have met criteria absent the CARES Act waiver) with specific handling for admissions before/after May 11, 2023 as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 — Remove cases with length of stay ≤ 7 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Trim applicable claims data to remove LTCH cases with a length of stay of 7 days or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short stays generally do not receive full LTCH treatment and including them would lower many relative weights and result in inappropriate payments; removal preserves integrity of average resource-use measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 — Establish low-volume MS-LTC-DRG quintiles
rubrics_metrics.description: For MS-LTC-DRGs with fewer than 25 applicable LTCH cases, group them into five quintiles based on average charge by sorting low-volume MS-LTC-DRGs in ascending order by average charge; assign each low-volume MS-LTC-DRG the relative weight and average length of stay of its quintile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the count of low-volume MS-LTC-DRGs is not evenly divisible by 5, assign remainder MS-LTC-DRGs to the quintile containing an MS-LTC-DRG with average charge closest to the remainder; monitor quintiles to avoid creating incentives for inappropriate admissions; adjust for any nonmonotonicity per Step 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 4 — Remove statistical outliers
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and remove statistical outlier cases from trimmed applicable LTCH cases: those outside 3.0 standard deviations from the mean of the log distribution of both charges per case and charges per day for each MS-LTC-DRG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outliers are removed because they may represent aberrations that distort average resource-use measures; removal precedes relative weight calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 5 — Adjust charges for Short Stay Outliers (SSOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust each LTCH's charges per discharge for remaining trimmed cases for the effects of SSOs by counting an SSO case as a fraction of a discharge equal to the ratio of the case's length of stay to the average length of stay of all cases in the MS-LTC-DRG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proportionate adjustment reduces the impact of lower charges for SSOs on MS-LTC-DRG average charges, avoiding underpayment of non-SSO cases and overpayment of SSOs; equivalent to adjusting SSO charges to the MS-LTC-DRG average LOS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 6 — Calculate relative weights using Hospital-Specific Relative Value (HSRV) iterative methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize charges by converting each LTCH's charge for an applicable case to a hospital-specific relative charge (divide adjusted case charge by LTCH average adjusted charge), multiply by the LTCH's case-mix index, and iteratively compute MS-LTC-DRG relative weights across LTCHs until convergence (initial case-mix index = 1.0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This accounts for nonrandom distribution of high/low charge cases across LTCHs by rescaling charges for LTCH average cost levels; compute SSO-adjusted average hospital-specific relative charge per MS-LTC-DRG and divide by overall SSO-adjusted average across all MS-LTC-DRGs to get the relative weight. Iterate updating LTCH case-mix and hospital-specific relative charge values until maximum difference between iterations is less than 0.0001.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 7 — Adjust relative weights to maintain monotonicity by severity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that within each base MS-LTC-DRG, relative weights increase by severity level (without CC/MCC < with CC < with MCC). When relative weights are nonmonotonic (higher severity has lower weight), combine severity levels or make adjustments to preserve monotonicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonmonotonic relative weights would produce inappropriate payments; apply historical methodology (see FY2010 IPPS/RY2010 final rule) to correct nonmonotonicity and document adjustments in Table 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 8 — Assign relative weights to no-volume MS-LTC-DRGs by clinical cross-walk
rubrics_metrics.description: For MS-LTC-DRGs with no trimmed applicable LTCH cases, cross-walk each no-volume MS-LTC-DRG to another MS-LTC-DRG for which a relative weight was calculated and assign the same relative weight and average length of stay, based on clinical similarity and relative costliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical similarity/costliness criteria include care during time surrounding surgery, surgical approach, procedure length, postoperative care, and length of stay. Exceptions include transplant MS-LTC-DRGs, error MS-LTC-DRGs, and psychiatric or rehabilitation MS-LTC-DRGs which are handled separately. If cross-walked MS-LTC-DRG is low-volume (in a quintile), assign the quintile relative weight. Adjust for nonmonotonicity when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 9 — Budget neutralize the uncapped relative weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust the set of uncapped relative weights by a normalization factor and a budget neutrality factor to ensure estimated aggregate LTCH PPS payments are unaffected by updates to classifications and relative weights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves budget neutrality for the annual update prior to applying any caps on weight changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 10 — Apply 10-percent cap on decreases in MS-LTC-DRG relative weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit the reduction of a MS-LTC-DRG's relative weight in a given year to no more than 10 percent of its prior year value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 10-percent cap policy does not apply to zero-volume MS-LTC-DRGs or low-volume MS-LTC-DRGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 11 — Budget neutralize the application of the 10-percent cap
rubrics_metrics.description: After applying the 10-percent cap to decreases, adjust the relative weights by a budget neutrality factor to ensure estimated aggregate LTCH PPS payments remain unaffected by the cap application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures overall payment neutrality after limiting individual MS-LTC-DRG decreases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and use of 'trimmed applicable LTCH cases'
rubrics_metrics.description: After removing LOS ≤ 7 days cases and statistical outliers, the remaining cases with length of stay ≥ 8 days are referred to as 'trimmed applicable LTCH cases' and are the basis for relative weight calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All subsequent steps (SSO adjustment, HSRV, quintile assignment, cross-walks) operate on trimmed applicable LTCH cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-walk assignment rationale and expected appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-walks are based on clinical similarity and relative costliness and are expected to yield appropriate payments in the rare event a few LTCH cases are grouped to a no-volume MS-LTC-DRG because the cross-walked MS-LTC-DRGs generally require equivalent relative resource use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to FY2010 IPPS/RY2010 final rule for more details on evaluating relative costliness; adjustments are made for nonmonotonicity as needed.
